title: BCD seven-segment driver
goal: Show BCD inputs driving labelled seven-segment outputs with gate-level logic for segments a and b.

rubric.must: Four inputs A, B, C, and D are visibly presented as the BCD input bus.
Seven distinct outputs labelled a through g are visible.
Segment a is visibly driven by inverted-input AND terms combined in an OR gate.
Segment b is visibly driven by its own multi-term AND-OR gate network.
Complemented versions of all four BCD inputs are visibly generated by inverter gates.

ideal.notes: Partial gate-level BCD to seven-segment driver in ANSI/IEEE Std 91 distinctive-shape symbols. The four BCD bits A, B, C and D enter on the left as the input bus; each drives a buffer that becomes one of the pass-through segment outputs c, d, e and f, and each also drops into an inverter, so all four complements nA, nB, nC and nD are generated. The bits and their complements then run down the sheet as labelled vertical literal rails. Segment a is the OR of three inverted-input AND terms a1, a2 and a3; segment b is the OR of its own three AND terms b1, b2 and b3; each term taps the rails for the literals it needs, with a filled dot at every connection. Segment g is the OR of A and B. All seven outputs a to g leave on the right margin. A wire that crosses a rail without a dot is not connected to it. Drawn in the idiom of the logic exemplar: ANSI/IEEE Std 91 distinctive shapes on one body box so the columns line up, ink-only palette with paper-filled gate bodies so a wire passing behind a gate is visibly interrupted, the gate type carried by the outline rather than printed under it, and the label slot spent on net names instead. Row pitch, channel x and canvas size are solved from browser-measured text widths, and the drawing was checked label-against-label, label-against-wire, label-against-canvas-edge and wire-against-every-unattached-gate before it was written: 0 collisions, and no wire crosses a gate body.
